precepts.text: Isaac called Jacob, blessed him, and charged him: thou shalt not take a wife of the daughters of Canaan; the fathers commanded their sons to choose from their own people.

note.label: Judges 14: An Occasion Against the Philistines

precepts.why:
Samson’s parents asked, “Is there never a woman among the daughters of thy brethren, or among all my people, that thou goest to take a wife of the uncircumcised Philistines?” They answered him rightly. The forefathers always charged their sons not to do this: “Isaac called Jacob, and blessed him, and charged him, and said unto him, Thou shalt not take a wife of the daughters of Canaan.”

The fathers commanded their sons to choose from their own people, and there were twelve tribes; there was no shortage of women in all the coasts of Israel. But as he grew up Samson had a lust issue with heathen women, the infamy the story of Samson is known for, and he insisted, “Get her for me; for she pleaseth me well.”

precepts.text: His thoughts are not our thoughts, neither are our ways his ways; his thoughts are higher than our thoughts.
precepts.point: The Most High is in control of everything, good and evil alike. Even affliction that comes on his people is his tactic to make them seek him and repent; nothing anybody does can alter the outcome he has already ordained, for he declared the end from the beginning.

note.label: Judges 14: An Occasion Against the Philistines

precepts.why: “his father and his mother knew not that it was of the Lord”. The Lord was moving Samson’s spirit, and the parents did not understand, just as we often question the Most High when we have no idea the depths of his wisdom and what he is really doing. “For my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways, saith the Lord. For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways, and my thoughts than your thoughts.” Who would think the Most High would use a man’s lust after Philistine women as an occasion against the Philistines, to destroy them for oppressing his people? His ways are higher than ours.

note.label: Judges 14: An Occasion Against the Philistines

precepts.why: “With him is strength and wisdom: the deceived and the deceiver are his.” Samson was deceived by the heathen women he lusted after, and later by Delilah; yet the deceived and the deceiver both belong to the Most High. He used these heathen women to get Samson caught up with the Philistines so that he would end up destroying them. Samson’s flaw was the occasion the Lord sought against the Philistines, who at that time had dominion over Israel. That is the basis of the whole story: the Lord was behind all of it, pulling the strings.

precepts.why: “There is no wisdom nor understanding nor counsel against the Lord.” The Philistines had dominion over Israel and Samson was chasing their daughters, yet none of it stood against the Lord: everything ultimately works within his plan. He sought an occasion against the Philistines through Samson’s own lust, and nothing anybody does, Samson, his parents or the Philistines, can alter the outcome he has already ordained, for he declared the end from the beginning.

The evil is wrong, but the Lord is behind it, working his purpose. precepts.text: In their affliction they will seek me early; affliction is how the Most High wakes his people up to repent.

note.label: Judges 14: An Occasion Against the Philistines

precepts.why: “I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face: in their affliction they will seek me early.” “at that time the Philistines had dominion over Israel”: that affliction was the Most High’s own tactic to make his people seek him and repent. Affliction is how the Most High wakes his people up. And the same Lord who let the Philistines have dominion was now seeking an occasion against them through Samson. Good and evil alike are in his control: he afflicts to bring repentance, and he avenges his people when the time comes.

points: What came of it: conflict with the Philistines, betrayal, thirty men dead, escalation into war, and in Judges 16 the loss of his vow, his strength, his eyes, and his freedom. A physical cautionary tale that men who move that way give up their preeminence. Attraction is the gateway to destruction if it is the only thing you move on.

note.label: Marriage Beyond Romance: From Eden to Modern Confusion

points: Samson saw a woman of the Philistines in Timnath and told his parents, get her for me to wife. They asked, is there never a woman among the daughters of thy brethren? He answered, get her for me, for she pleaseth me well. Purely visual reasoning, like the brother who sees nothing he likes in his congregation and grabs one online or in another city, hoping she will understand all this later.

note.label: Judges 14: An Occasion Against the Philistines

points: As Samson went down to the vineyards of Timnath, a young lion roared against him, challenging him. Here you begin to see the divine power on Samson.

note.label: Judges 14: An Occasion Against the Philistines

points: The spirit of the Lord came mightily upon him, and he rent the lion as he would have rent a kid, and he had nothing in his hand: no weapon, no sword, nothing. He tore up a young lion, a prince of the jungle, like it was a little goat. This is one of the forms of the spirit of the Lord, spiritual power.
He told not his father or his mother what he had done; he did not boast about it.

note.label: Judges 14: An Occasion Against the Philistines

points: He went down and talked with the woman, and she pleased Samson well.

note.label: Judges 14: An Occasion Against the Philistines

points: After a time he returned to take her, and he turned aside to see the carcase of the lion he had slain, and behold, there was a swarm of bees and honey in the carcase.

note.label: Judges 14: An Occasion Against the Philistines

points: He took of the honey in his hands and went on eating, and gave to his father and mother and they did eat, but he told them not that he had taken the honey out of the carcase of the lion.

note.label: Judges 14: An Occasion Against the Philistines

points: His father went down unto the woman, and Samson made there a feast, as the young men used to do, and when the Philistines saw him they brought thirty companions to be with him.

note.label: Judges 14: An Occasion Against the Philistines

points: Samson put forth a riddle: if they could declare it within the seven days of the feast, he would give them thirty sheets and thirty change of garments, and if they could not, they would give him the same.

note.label: Judges 14: An Occasion Against the Philistines

points: The riddle: out of the eater came forth meat, and out of the strong came forth sweetness. In three days they could not expound it.

note.label: Judges 14: An Occasion Against the Philistines

points: On the seventh day they said unto Samson's wife, entice thy husband that he may declare unto us the riddle, lest we burn thee and thy father's house with fire. They threatened to burn their own countrywoman in her father's house over thirty outfits.

note.label: Judges 14: An Occasion Against the Philistines

points: She turned to manipulation and wept before him: thou dost but hate me, and lovest me not; thou hast put forth a riddle unto the children of my people and hast not told it me. He answered, I have not told it my father nor my mother, and shall I tell it thee?

note.label: Judges 14: An Occasion Against the Philistines

points: She wept before him the seven days while their feast lasted, and on the seventh day he told her, because she lay sore upon him. This big strong mighty brother caved in because of the tears of a woman.

note.label: Judges 14: An Occasion Against the Philistines

points: She told the riddle to the children of her people, and the men of the city answered him before the sun went down: what is sweeter than honey, and what is stronger than a lion?
Samson knew exactly what happened: if ye had not plowed with my heifer, ye had not found out my riddle.

Never trust your enemy. That was his wife, and her loyalty belonged to him, but when she got the riddle out of him she went and told it to her heathen people, his enemy. That is why it makes no sense to marry the enemy.

note.label: Judges 14: An Occasion Against the Philistines

points: The spirit of the Lord came upon him, and he went down to Ashkelon and slew thirty men of the Philistines, took their spoil, and gave the change of garments unto them which expounded the riddle; the spirit of the Lord came upon him even for this, against the nation that oppressed Israel.

note.label: Judges 14: An Occasion Against the Philistines

points: His anger was kindled, and he went up to his father's house, and Samson's wife was given to his companion, whom he had used as his friend; she was his wife to be, for they had not yet consummated the marriage.
